intent: A dark, premium studio footer that closes the page with a big line, link columns, a newsletter, a live local clock, and a giant wordmark measured to span the container exactly and cut off above its baseline. It reveals once on scroll: rules draw, words and columns stagger out of a blur, the clock counts up, and the wordmark rises out of the floor.

stack.styling: Tailwind CSS v4 with container queries (@container on the footer)
stack.animation: motion/react: variants on one shared reveal timeline (useInView per block), pathLength rings, motion-value clock
stack.fonts: font-display (Geist, tight tracking), font-sans (Geist), font-mono (Geist Mono)

layout.container: footer is the @container; inner max-w-[1440px], px 20/32/48, pt 64/80/96
rows: closing line + large mailto link; back-to-top ring button on the right from @3xl (768px)
2px white/15% rule; grid 2 -> 4 (@2xl) -> 12 (@6xl, 1152px): Studio, Work, Elsewhere, Visit (2 cols each) + newsletter (cols 9-12; full row split copy/form at @2xl-@5xl)
1px white/8% rule; legal line + legal links in mono, split from @5xl
fitted wordmark flush to both container edges, cut 14% above the baseline

color.tokens: one COLORS object exposed as CSS variables
color.wordmark: vertical metal gradient #ffffff 90% → #a1a1aa 50% → #3f3f46 5% (gradient id from useId)
color.hairline: top hairline fading out at both ends; no glow, no radial light, no accent colour

motion.reveal: four blocks (closing line, column grid, wordmark, legal bar), each once at 25% visible; a shared clock keeps blocks that arrive together in order while one scrolled to later starts at once. Items rise 12px out of an 8px blur, 600ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)
motion.lead: top hairline draws from the centre; headline words 35ms apart; email at 300ms with its underline drawing left→right; arrow chip pops (scale .6→1) at 420ms; back-to-top ring draws along its path (pathLength, 700ms) from 240ms, arrow and label follow
motion.grid: slot 320ms: the 2px rule draws; each column 60ms after the last, its title then links 30ms apart; Visit: address, then the live dot pops and starts pinging, then the clock counts from 00:00 to local time over 700ms with tabular figures and a 3px blur settle; the newsletter lands last
motion.wordmark: slot 500ms: rises from fully below the floor (translate in viewBox units) over 1.1s on a slow-start cubic-bezier(0.6,0,0.2,1) so the climb stays on screen, and fades and sharpens from an 8px blur over 900ms on the shared ease, once measured
motion.legal: slot 620ms: rule draws, legal line, links 30ms apart
motion.links: background-size underline grows from the left (300ms); the email underline retracts to the right on hover (400ms)
motion.chips: arrow chip rotates -45deg on hover; back-to-top arrow lifts 4px
motion.newsletter: AnimatePresence mode=wait: form exits up 8px, success pill rises 8px out of a 4px blur over 0.4s and its check draws
motion.clock: ticks on each minute boundary (one timeout, no per-second polling); the dot's ping is the one ambient signal and only runs while on screen
motion.reducedMotion: 150ms fades only; clock set instantly; no rise, blur, ping; back-to-top scrolls instantly
motion.press: buttons and links press to 0.97, the email to 0.99, 150ms

responsive.mobile: 2-col link grid, newsletter full width, back-to-top row under the email, wordmark about 50px tall at 390px
responsive.@3xl: back-to-top moves to the right of the closing line

accessibility: each link column is a nav with aria-label
address element; time element with dateTime
sr-only input label, aria-invalid, polite live error, role=status success
external links marked (opens in a new tab)

content.headline: Got a brief, a hunch or a half-built thing?
content.clock: London, Europe/London (the city label defaults to the last part of the time zone, underscores as spaces, when omitted)
content.newsletter: Low Tide: a short letter every other Thursday

avoid: sizing the wordmark with a guessed vw value
saturated slabs, glow or radial light
equal-weight tiny link columns with no hierarchy
a pulsing clock colon (one ambient signal only)
revealing the whole footer as one block
